skill.name: dcg
skill.description: Destructive Command Guard adds a Claude Code hook that blocks known destructive shell commands before execution.
skill.summary: Blocks risky Claude Code shell commands before they can delete work or rewrite history.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown examples that document commands DCG blocks or allows, so they are false positives. Confirmed risks remain in remote pipe-to-shell installation, the sudo installer path, external code fetching, and hidden Claude Code hook configuration.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell installation with signed release downloads, checksums, or package manager distribution. Avoid cache-busting install URLs.
Avoid sudo during install. Prefer a user-level install and document exact files changed before requesting elevated privileges.
Require manual confirmation before editing Claude Code settings. Document the hook trust boundary and the exact command that will run.
Make coverage limits prominent. Offer a stricter mode for teams that need fail-closed command handling.

semantic_findings.title: Documented Guard Bypass Mechanism
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents DCG_BYPASS=1 and manual execution as bypass paths. This is useful for overrides, but it weakens enforcement if users expect a hard sandbox.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The bypass variable and manual bypass guidance are explicitly documented. The risk is contextual because bypass controls are intentional but reduce protection guarantees.

semantic_findings.title: Default-Allow Coverage Gap
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that unrecognized commands are allowed and that non-Bash commands and script contents are not inspected. Users should not treat this as complete command sandboxing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The limitations are directly stated in the skill documentation. The finding is about protection coverage, not hidden malicious intent.

content.value_statement: AI coding agents can run commands that delete work or rewrite history. DCG adds a Claude Code hook that blocks known destructive commands before execution.
actual_capabilities: Registers as a Claude Code PreToolUse hook for Bash commands.
Blocks documented destructive git commands, force pushes, stash deletion, and risky recursive removal.
Uses whitelist-first matching so known safe command variants can pass.
Documents modular packs for databases, containers, Kubernetes, cloud tools, and infrastructure tools.
Supports environment controls for pack selection, verbosity, colors, and bypass behavior.
Provides manual test guidance for checking whether a command would be blocked.
limitations: The submitted skill contains documentation only; implementation code is fetched from an external repository.
Unknown commands are allowed by default, so coverage depends on maintained patterns.
The guard covers Claude Code Bash hooks and does not inspect non-Bash tools or script internals.
Users can bypass the guard with the documented environment variable or by running commands manually.

use_cases.title: Prevent accidental repository damage
use_cases.description: Block destructive git and removal commands before an AI coding agent can run them.
use_cases.target_user: Developers using Claude Code on active repositories

use_cases.description: Install a pre-command safety layer for repeated automation tasks and long coding sessions.

use_cases.description: Assess which command families are blocked, allowed, or outside the hook threat model.

best_practices: Use a user-level install and verify release artifacts before enabling the hook.
Enable only the packs that match tools used in the repository.

anti_patterns: Do not use remote pipe-to-shell installation in shared or production environments.
Do not rely on DCG as a sandbox for malicious commands.
Do not enable broad bypass settings during normal agent work.

faq.question: What does DCG protect?
faq.answer: It blocks known destructive Bash commands before Claude Code runs them.

faq.question: Does DCG stop every dangerous command?
faq.answer: No. It allows unknown commands by default and does not inspect non-Bash tools.

faq.question: Why does it use a Claude Code hook?
faq.answer: The hook lets DCG inspect Bash tool requests before execution.

faq.question: Can users override a block?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation includes a bypass variable and manual execution guidance.

faq.question: Is the submitted skill self-contained?
faq.answer: No. The skill file documents an external Rust project and installer.

faq.question: Should teams allow automatic installation?
faq.answer: No. Teams should review the remote installer and prefer verified release artifacts.
